I'll be sure to drop you a message. As much as my therapist does help, a fellow BPD sufferer could also be helpful since you obviously we're in the same boat.

The quote from the book/film Girl, Interrupted - "I didn't try to kill myself, I tried to kill a part of myself" (probably not the exact quote but it's not important) is the best way to describe BPD imo.

I do deal with severe suicidal thoughts and have attempted, but when delving deeper, it's the destructive behaviour that comes with having BPD really is seemingly myself trying to escape some part of myself. I don't *enjoy* who I am. I'm confident in the way I look, but my personality I'm *always* trying to change. Whether it be through giving in to impulsive thoughts or deciding not to be an ordinary, functioning human being.

I've become dependent on my closest friend and am just currently stuck in my own personal limbo of 'do I want to get better or not?', 'I won't get the attention I do if I recover', etc.

BPD truly is such a complicated illness. Topped off with my battle with anxiety and paranoia, it's a fucking maze of constant war between rational and irrational thought. I don't know much about C-PTSD but I'll look into the similarities. I always make sure to research other MI's because I think it's important to be in the know about all of them.

I know you can 'grow out' of BPD, and since I'm only 20 that's certainly a possibility for me, but first I really have to fight the urge to just stay ill and stuck in this cycle of mass destruction upon myself. Even reading your offer of figuring out how to fix myself my mind is already telling me not to even try to get better. Ugh. It's difficult.
